newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich followed House lawyer's advice - report.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich followed House lawyer's advice - report.

text.p: Despite his own attorneys' warnings, House Speaker Newt Gingrich relied on advice from a House ethics lawyer in deciding to finance his college course through a tax-exempt foundation, a newspaper said on Saturday.

The Atlanta Journal-Constitution quoted a Gingrich aide as saying a Republican attorney working for the House ethics committee told the speaker in 1993 he saw no law or tax regulation that would conflict with plans for the course, called "Renewing American Civilisation."
"As Newt stated to the committee, he sought and obtained legal counsel throughout the process of setting up his course," Gingrich spokesman Tony Blankley told the newspaper.

But the House attorney, David McCarthy, was primarily concerned with what roles the speaker and his congressional staff would play in the course. He had little interest in the outside advisers, whose roles have since fallen under House scrutiny, the newspaper said.

The Gingrich aide's remarks came in response to a Friday article in the Journal-Constitution, which said two attorneys had warned the Georgia Republican in 1990 about involving charitable or educational foundations in political projects.

"Renewing American Civilisation," which was taught at two small colleges in Georgia and distributed nationwide on videocassette, was part of a partisan effort to spread Gingrich's political message, according to the House ethics panel's investigating subcommittee.

The ethics committee will consider what penalty, if any, to impose on the speaker. Republicans, who have mostly rallied behind Gingrich, were hoping the penalty phase would be concluded before the House votes Jan. 7 on re-electing him as speaker. Some Democrats have called for Gingrich to step down.
